problems.title: Intersections of reciprocal cubics
problems.question: How many intersections have y=−x³ and y=−1/x³?
problems.idea: Equate the values with x≠0.
steps: The real roots are x=1 and x=−1, giving two distinct intersections.

problems.title: The point at two asymptotes
problems.question: Through A, neither the horizontal nor vertical line intersects f(x)=(x−199)/(x−200). Find A.
problems.idea: Identify the missing input and missing output.
steps: No point of the graph has x=200 or y=1. Every other vertical and horizontal line meets it.

problems.title: Intersections of two powers
problems.question: How many intersections have y=x⁵ and y=x¹²?
problems.idea: Factor their equality.
steps: The real solutions are x=0 and x=1.

problems.title: Area of a trapezoid from two diagonal triangles
problems.question: Diagonals meet at O. Triangles on the parallel bases have areas 18 and 2. Find the trapezoid area.
problems.idea: The two remaining triangles each have the geometric-mean area.
steps: The mixed triangles each have area √(18·2)=6, by equal altitudes and diagonal ratios.

problems.title: Area from a side and two medians
problems.question: One triangle side is 10; medians to the other sides are 15 and 18. Find its area.
problems.idea: The centroid creates a triangle with two thirds of each median and the known side.
formulas: Centroid triangle sides=10,12,10; its area is one third of the original.
steps: Its altitude to the side 12 is √(10²−6²)=8, so its area is 48.
The original area is 3·48.

problems.title: A nested fourth, third and square root
problems.question: Simplify $\sqrt[4]{x\sqrt[3]{x\sqrt{x}}}$.
problems.idea: Use fractional exponents with x≥0.
steps: The expression is x³ᐟ⁸, including x=0.
problems.answer: The eighth root of x³, for x≥0.

problems.title: Put a factor inside a cube root
problems.question: Simplify x·∛(−x).
problems.idea: Odd roots allow signed factors to move inside.
steps: The product is ∛(−x⁴), valid for every real x.

problems.title: Extract a power from an even root
problems.question: Simplify −⁴√(−a⁹) over the reals.
problems.idea: Its domain forces a≤0.
steps: The leading negative sign stays outside.
Thus the expression is −a²·⁴√(−a)=−a²·⁴√|a|.

problems.title: A rhombus inside a parallelogram
problems.question: A rhombus has vertices on a parallelogram’s sides and sides parallel to its diagonals. The diagonal ratio is 2. Find their area ratio.
problems.idea: Use the diagonal directions as coordinate axes.
formulas: For diagonal lengths p,q, rhombus side l satisfies l/p+l/q=1, so l=pq/(p+q).
steps: The rhombus area is l²sinθ; the parallelogram area is pq sinθ/2, where θ is the angle between diagonals.
Their ratio is 2pq/(p+q)². At p=2q it is 4/9.

problems.title: Area from two tangency lengths and an angle
problems.question: An incircle splits one side into lengths 3 and 1. The opposite angle is 120°. Find the triangle area.
problems.idea: Represent all sides by equal tangent segments.
formulas: Let third vertex’s tangent length be t. Sides are 4,3+t,1+t; semiperimeter=4+t.
steps: The cosine rule at 120° gives 16=(3+t)²+(1+t)²+(3+t)(1+t), hence t²+4t=1.
The inradius is t tan60°=√3t.

problems.title: Negative values of a shifted square root
problems.question: For which x is y=√(x+1)−3 negative?
problems.idea: Require the radicand’s domain as well as the inequality.
steps: Intersect the two conditions.

problems.title: Monotonicity of a shifted cube root
problems.question: Find the increasing interval of y=∛(x−2)+3.
problems.idea: A real cube root is strictly increasing on its whole domain.
steps: Horizontal and vertical shifts preserve that increasing behavior.

problems.title: Inverse of a linear function
problems.question: Find the inverse of y=2x−1.
problems.idea: Solve for x and interchange the variable names.
steps: The inverse takes an input x to (x+1)/2.

problems.title: An altitude equals the mean of two others
problems.question: Two triangle sides are 2 and 4. The altitude to the third side equals the arithmetic mean of the altitudes to those two sides. Find the third side.
problems.idea: All altitudes have the same area numerator.

problems.title: Area of a trapezoid with four known sides
problems.question: A trapezoid has legs 13,20 and bases 1,22. Find its area.
problems.idea: The leg projections onto the larger base sum to 21.
formulas: Let projections be u,v. u+v=21, v²−u²=20²−13²=231.
steps: Thus v−u=11, giving u=5,v=16.
Height=√(13²−5²)=12.

problems.title: A monotonicity question with two valid choices
problems.question: Which listed transformation has increasing interval equal to the decreasing interval of f(x)=3x+1?
problems.idea: f is strictly increasing and has no decreasing interval.
steps: Both displayed functions are strictly decreasing everywhere, so neither has an increasing interval.
Their empty increasing sets agree with the empty decreasing set of f. The absolute-value options do have increasing portions.
problems.answer: Both f(−x) and −f(x), corresponding to options b and e.
problems.note: The printed question has two valid choices if empty monotonicity intervals are allowed. If it requires a nonempty interval, none qualifies.

problems.title: Range after taking absolute values
problems.question: The range of f is [−9,4]. Find the range of |f|.
problems.idea: Fold negative outputs onto the nonnegative axis.
steps: Zero is attained, and every value up to 9 is attained from the original negative outputs.

problems.title: Domain after an absolute-value input
problems.question: The domain of f is [−9,4]. Find the domain of f(|x|).
problems.idea: The new input |x| must remain in the original domain.
steps: Thus −4≤x≤4.

problems.title: A triangle inside a trapezoid
problems.question: M is midpoint of base AD. BM meets AC at K. The trapezoid area is 280 and the larger base AD is six times BC. Find area AKM.
problems.idea: Use similarity to locate K along AC.
formulas: Write BC=b, AD=6b, AM=3b. Then AK/KC=AM/BC=3, so height of K=3h/4.
steps: Trapezoid area=7bh/2=280, so bh=80.
The desired area is 9·80/8.
problems.note: This is the intended result when AD is the larger base. The wording gives only a base ratio of 6 without identifying the larger base; if BC=6AD instead, the area would be 20/13.

problems.title: Perpendicular diagonals of a trapezoid
problems.question: A trapezoid has perpendicular diagonals, one of length 9, and midline 7.5. Find the other diagonal.
problems.idea: The vector difference of the diagonals is the sum of the bases.
steps: 9²+d₂²=15², so d₂²=144.

problems.title: An odd periodic function with an endpoint inconsistency
problems.question: An odd function has period 4 and f(x)=3x²−x on [0,2]. Find f(199).
problems.idea: Reduce the argument modulo the period, then use oddness.
steps: f(1)=3−1=2, so the intended f(199)=−2.
However, the endpoint formula gives f(2)=10, while period 4 and oddness require f(2)=f(−2)=−f(2), hence f(2)=0.
problems.note: No function satisfies all the stated conditions at the endpoints. The intended calculation works if the given formula applies on 0≤x<2 instead.

problems.title: An angle bisector and an area ratio
problems.question: AB=3, AC=8, AD bisects A, and DE∥AB with E on AC. Find area ADE divided by area ABC.
problems.idea: Use the angle-bisector ratio and the similar triangle CDE.
steps: Thus AE/AC=3/11. Triangles ACD and ABC share altitude from A, so their area ratio is CD/CB=8/11.
Within ACD, triangles ADE and ACD share altitude from D, giving ratio AE/AC=3/11.
Multiply the two ratios.

problems.title: Integer and fractional parts
problems.question: Which number solves floor(x)={x}+19.9?
problems.idea: Write x=n+t with integer n and 0≤t<1.
steps: The only integer in [19.9,20.9) is n=20, giving t=0.1.
Thus x=20.1.

problems.title: An altitude and median trisect an angle
problems.question: An altitude and a median from one vertex divide its angle into three equal parts. In what ratio do they divide the area?
problems.idea: The median divides the total area into two equal halves.
formulas: Triangles sharing the vertex have areas proportional to their base segments.
steps: Let the altitude foot split one of those halves. The two adjacent right triangles at the altitude have equal vertex angles, so their base segments and areas are equal.
The remaining region is the other median half, twice either smaller region.

problems.title: A cyclic trapezoid with three equal sides
problems.question: A cyclic trapezoid has circumradius 2/√3. Its larger base is twice each of its other three sides. Find that base.
problems.idea: Such a cyclic trapezoid is isosceles.
formulas: Let the three equal sides be s, larger base 2s. Height=√(s²−(s/2)²)=√3s/2.
steps: Coordinates of the vertices can be (±s,0),(±s/2,√3s/2). Each is distance s from the origin, so its circumradius is s.
Thus larger base=2R.
